newsitem.title: GERMANY: AMB-Reuters German Advertising & Media Digest-Apr16.
newsitem.headline: AMB-Reuters German Advertising & Media Digest-Apr16.

text.p: REUTERS GERMAN ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST
News from the Reuters and the German press on Advertising,
Marketing, Brand-name Products, Media and the Internet
ADVERTISING & MARKETING:
WOLFSBURG - Volkswagen says the first new advertising campaign
under a recently renewed ad account with Duesseldorf agency DDB
Needham will be to unveil its new VW Golf model. (Reuter)
FRANKFURT - The German advertisers' association (GWA)
reorganises its media board. (Reuter)
MEDIA & THE INTERNET:
GUETERSLOH - Media group Bertelsmanmnn says its plans to offer
network services abroad using Internet technology. The company
says it will work with U.S.-based ANS Communications to form
European subsidiaries which would offer large customers
telecommunication services.
(Reuter)
STUTTGART - Most German publishers do not believe the boom in
electronic media has harmed their traditional business, says
industry survey. The poll was conducted by the Fraunhofer
Institute for Labour Market and Organisation (IAO), in which 500
German publishers were asked to give their views on trends in
the industry in light of the rise of electronic news media in
publishing. (Reuter)
BRAND-NAME PRODUCTS & MARKETS:
MUNICH - Luxury car maker BMW posted 22-percent boost in
turnover in the first quarter of 1997 to 13.98 billion
marks($8.10 billion). British unit Rover Group contributed 3.6
billion marks of those sales. (Reuter)
BREMEN - German medium-sized electronics retailers have joined
forces against the Media-Markt chain, says a federation of
stores in Bremen, Bremerhaven, Bamberg and Bayreuth. The
retailers say Media-Markt, a unit of Metro-Konzern, has for
years systematically brought lawsuits against its competitors
for minor infractions. (Reuter)
FRANKFURT - German airline Deutsche Lufthansa AG has confirmed
it is planning to restructure its sales organisation as part of
a previously-announced move to cut some 10 percent of its
management and administration positions. (Reuter)
HAMBURG - Textiles retailer Jean Pascale says it increased
sales in 1996 by one percent to 410 million marks. The company
says its surplus for the year sank to one million marks from a
1995 sum of 12.48 million marks. (Reuter)
Deborah Cole, Berlin Newsroom, 49-30-203-98114
